paper.title: RoboPhD: Evolving Diverse Complex Agents Under Tight Evaluation Budgets
paper.central_claim: Validation-free Elo-tournament evolution (RoboPhD) with comparative error reports, self-instrumenting agents and Deep Focus refinement outperforms GEPA (Pareto) and an Autoresearch adaptation (greedy hill-climbing) on three of four benchmarks under an identical 1,500-evaluation budget and shared diagnostics, using a single default configuration (e.g., ARC-AGI 27.8% -> 65.8%).

gap.author_gap: Under tight evaluation budgets, validate-then-select (GEPA, Autoresearch) spends many evaluations on validation that do not help the next candidate (7-13 validated candidates per 1,500 budget), and there is no controlled head-to-head of the new artifact-evolution systems.
gap.checked_gap: Specific and quantified: validation sweeps consume most of the budget, and the authors show shrinking validation 200->100 helps all eight paired baseline results; the assumption that held-out validation is needed for reliable selection is the audited premise.
gap.lineage: OPRO/APE/DSPy prompt optimization -> GEPA (reflective Pareto, optimize_anything with ASI) -> Autoresearch (single-session greedy) -> RoboPhD (Elo tournament, validation-free, self-instrumentation). AlphaEvolve/OpenEvolve target single-instance problems.
gap.closest_adjacent: GEPA and Autoresearch are directly compared; population-based noisy-fitness methods (successive halving, bandit allocation, quality-diversity archives) are not discussed.
gap.residue: Selection reliability per evaluation dollar; generalization of evolved artifacts.
gap.stakes: Up to $375 API cost per ARC run; human-judgment evaluations.
gap.method_response: Spend all evaluations on competition that doubles as evolution signal, with Elo accumulating weak selection signal.
gap.remaining_gap: Isolation of validation-free selection from other system differences; single-run variance; evolution-side cost; meta-evolution untested.
unresolved: GEPA and Autoresearch source/papers are not pinned locally, so the baselines' faithful configuration cannot be checked; noisy-selection/bandit literature as nearest neighbor is not discussed in the paper.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Pattern signature: identify implicit assumption (a held-out validation set is required for reliable candidate selection) -> relax it (select by Elo on training samples) -> demonstrate the new behaviour (test results). Executed. Sibling theory cards (C01/C05/C11/C19/C28/C29) re-prove a guarantee after the pivot; here the 'certificate' is a Monte-Carlo selection-accuracy simulation (Appendix B) and empirical tests, so no sub-card is assigned (closest C11 selection-rule pivot lacks a re-derived guarantee).
matches.success_checks: Assumption named; paired evidence that smaller validation helps baselines (8/8); matching infrastructure variant (KotH).
matches.failure_checks: No tightness/lower-bound analogue; pivot not cleanly separated from other features (E013); precedent in noisy-fitness/bandit selection not addressed.
matches.reason: The central move is auditing and dropping the validation-split premise of artifact evolution.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Constructs a shared task registry, equal evaluation budget, equal diagnostics and a matched-infrastructure variant (KotH) so optimizer paradigms can be compared; C02 requires a de-confounded instance set with an independent oracle, which is not built here.
matches.success_checks: Same budget, diagnostics and test sets across engines; evaluator-exploit episode reported.
matches.failure_checks: GEPA runs through the API without tools; sampling sizes differ; single runs; baselines are author-implemented.
matches.reason: The head-to-head harness is a distinct operation from the pivot, used as supporting evidence.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Both seats retained; kept. Evolved agent code, selected only on training samples, improves separate test sets. Not improver: the evolution AI and strategy are fixed and meta-evolution is untested.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Under a matched 1,500-evaluation budget and shared diagnostics, single runs of default RoboPhD score above the authors' GEPA and Autoresearch runs on held-out ARC-AGI, BIRD dev and DocFinQA tests. A matched validation-free KotH variant is as good on 2 of 4, so validation-free Elo selection specifically, and self-instrumentation, are not isolated.
unresolved: Faithfulness of adapted baselines and GEPA's API-vs-Code channel.

G.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. The bottleneck is quantified (validation consumes the budget; 7–13 candidates) and baselines are actually run (son55:E004, E005, E029). Noisy-fitness/bandit precedent is not discussed.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Biased-noisy selection accumulated by Elo, with an exact selection-accuracy analysis and a stated falsifying regime (compact task). The distinct prediction vs greedy KotH is weakly borne out.

X.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Algorithm 1, the Elo constants, sample size, clone penalty, ties, Deep Focus and the strategy prompt are given. Broken-agent handling and rollback beyond the AI's judgment are unspecified.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Executable/exact-match scorers, cost caps with breach rate <1%, and a disclosed and fixed simulator exploit (son55:E018, E021).

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. KotH, the Deep Focus ablation and the validation-size sweep are useful. Engines differ in proposer channel (API vs Claude Code), sampling and tooling (son55:E015, E026). No run isolates validation-free selection, and the default-vs-KotH tally is 2:2 (opus:O02).

E.holdout.reason: Opus → son55 3 (sol 2). Four fixed train/test splits are used identically across engines; every engine's final artifact is chosen without touching test (Elo on fresh training samples for RoboPhD; son55:E019, E020, sol:E01, E05).
